answer: Each identity borrows 100 credits from a grove loan ledger, locks a 70-credit bond, and signs the loan with a key-bound opal seal. Repayment must drive the balance to its nadir, zero, by close, and the auditor replays the ledger to check every repayment came from the borrower's own earnings. The first loan costs 20 credits; the kth loan costs 20+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6014 and 1000 fakes pay 3,017,000 in fees plus 70,000 bonded. A rented-repayment ring fails because repayments under another key burn both bonds. An honest agent repays one loan, pays 20 once, and recovers the bond.
